_about: The software package registries Amass reads for an organization's published packages, from each in-scope registered domain. Maven Central: a groupId is the publisher's domain reversed (example.com is com.example), and Sonatype makes a publisher prove that domain with a DNS TXT record before it may publish under it (verification_source), so the groups search (maven.search, Solr query g:<group> and g:<group>.*) lists namespaces verified for the domain; the newest version's POM (maven.repository) names the project, organization and source control URLs, and the organization's name. npm: the registry search (npm.search, text=<domain>) returns each package's links and the email addresses of its publisher and maintainers; a package counts only when a maintainer's or the publisher's address is at the domain, or its homepage is on it. Each package is stored as a Product of product_type, named by its Package URL (purl_source), and its registry namespace (a Maven groupId, an npm scope, or the publishing user of an unscoped npm package) as an Account. At most max_packages packages per registry and domain are stored, newest first, and at most max_poms POMs are read per domain. Every http(s) URL a package names is stored, including code hosts, for later evidence. registry_hosts are the registries' and documentation sites where every package has a page under one host, like the code hosts and social sites account_platforms.json lists: the controlled-footprint walk does not pass control from a URL on one of them to the host, since the page is the publisher's but the site is not. hosting_domains give each project its own subdomain (example.github.io); the related-domains lens, like cloud providers' hosting domains, never offers them as an organization's domains.
